sanskrit: dīrghāyur atha vālpāyuḥ saguṇo nirguṇo 'pi vā sakṛd vṛto mayā bhartā na dvitīyaṃ vṛṇomy aham
english: Whether long-lived or short-lived, whether endowed with virtues or lacking them — a husband once chosen by me, I shall not choose a second time.

sanskrit: manasā niścayaṃ kṛtvā tato vācābhidhīyate kriyate karmaṇā paścāt pramāṇaṃ me manas tataḥ
english: A resolve formed first in the mind is then declared in speech, and afterward carried out in deed; the mind is therefore my authority.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sthirā buddhir naraśreṣṭha sāvitryā duhitus tava naiṣā cālayituṃ śakyā dharmād asmāt kathaṃ cana
english: Nārada said: The understanding of Sāvitrī, your daughter, O best of men, is firm; she cannot by any means be turned away from this dharma.

sanskrit: nānyasmin puruṣe santi ye satyavati vai guṇāḥ pradānam eva tasmān me rocate duhitus tava
english: The qualities that Satyavān possesses are not found in any other man. Therefore the giving away of your daughter pleases me.

sanskrit: rājovāca avicāryam etad uktaṃ hi tathyaṃ bhagavatā vacaḥ kariṣyāmy etad evaṃ ca gurur hi bhagavān mama
english: The king said: What has been spoken by the blessed one is true and beyond deliberation; I shall do exactly this, for you, O blessed one, are my guru.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca avighnam astu sāvitryāḥ pradāne duhitus tava sādhayiṣyāmahe tāvat sarveṣāṃ bhadram astu vaḥ
english: Nārada said: May the giving of your daughter Sāvitrī be free of obstacles. We shall accomplish it. May good befall all of you.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktvā kham utpatya nāradas tridivaṃ gataḥ rājāpi duhituḥ sarvaṃ vaivāhikam akārayat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, Nārada soared into the sky and departed to heaven. The king too made all the wedding preparations for his daughter.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atha kanyāpradāne sa tam evārthaṃ vicintayan samāninye ca tat sarvaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ vaivāhikaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, reflecting on that very matter of giving away his daughter, the king assembled all the requisite goods for the wedding.

sanskrit: tato vṛddhān dvijān sarvān ṛtvijaḥ sapurohitān samāhūya tithau puṇye prayayau saha kanyayā
english: Then, having summoned all the elder twice-born, the officiating priests, and the family chaplain, he set out with his daughter on an auspicious day.

sanskrit: medhyāraṇyaṃ sa gatvā ca dyumatsenāśramaṃ nṛpaḥ padbhyām eva dvijaiḥ sārdhaṃ rājarṣiṃ tam upāgamat
english: Arriving at the sacred forest, the king proceeded on foot together with the brahmins and approached the hermitage of Dyumatsena, that royal sage.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyan mahābhāgaṃ śālavṛkṣam upāśritam kauśyāṃ bṛsyāṃ samāsīnaṃ cakṣurhīnaṃ nṛpaṃ tadā
english: There they saw the greatly fortunate blind king sitting on a cushion of kuśa grass, leaning against a śāla tree.

sanskrit: sa rājā tasya rājarṣeḥ kṛtvā pūjāṃ yathārhataḥ vācā suniyato bhūtvā cakārātmanivedanam
english: That king paid homage to the royal sage as was fitting and, restraining his speech carefully, introduced himself.

sanskrit: tasyārghyam āsanaṃ caiva gāṃ cāvedya sa dharmavit kim āgamanam ity evaṃ rājā rājānam abravīt
english: That knower of dharma offered him the arghya, a seat, and a cow, and then the king asked the other king: "What is the purpose of your coming?"

sanskrit: tasya sarvam abhiprāyam itikartavyatāṃ ca tām satyavantaṃ samuddiśya sarvam eva nyavedayat
english: He disclosed to him his entire intention and the entire course of action to be done, directing it all toward Satyavān.

sanskrit: aśvapatir uvāca sāvitrī nāma rājarṣe kanyeyaṃ mama śobhanā tāṃ svadharmeṇa dharmajña snuṣārthe tvaṃ gṛhāṇa me
english: Aśvapati said: O royal sage, this lovely daughter of mine is named Sāvitrī. O knower of dharma, receive her from me according to proper rite as a daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca cyutāḥ sma rājyād vanavāsam āśritāś; carāma dharmaṃ niyatās tapasvinaḥ kathaṃ tv anarhā vanavāsam āśrame; sahiṣyate kleśam imaṃ sutā tava
english: Dyumatsena said: We have been deprived of our kingdom and have taken to forest life; we practice dharma with discipline as ascetics. How shall your daughter, who is undeserving of such hardship, endure this toil in the hermitage?

sanskrit: aśvapatir uvāca sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca bhavābhavātmakaṃ; yadā vijānāti sutāham eva ca na madvidhe yujyati vākyam īdṛśaṃ; viniścayenābhigato 'smi te nṛpa
english: Aśvapati said: When my daughter and I both understand that joy and sorrow are of the nature of coming and going, such words do not befit one like me. I have come to you with firm resolve, O king.

sanskrit: āśāṃ nārhasi me hantuṃ sauhṛdād praṇayena ca abhitaś cāgataṃ premṇā pratyākhyātuṃ na mārhasi
english: You ought not to destroy my hope out of friendship and affection; you should not refuse one who has come to you from all sides with love.

sanskrit: anurūpo hi saṃyoge tvaṃ mamāhaṃ tavāpi ca snuṣāṃ pratīccha me kanyāṃ bhāryāṃ satyavataḥ sutām
english: We are indeed well-matched for this union — you for me and I for you. Accept my daughter as a daughter-in-law, as a wife for Satyavān.

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca pūrvam evābhilaṣitaḥ saṃbandho me tvayā saha bhraṣṭarājyas tv aham iti tata etad vicāritam
english: Dyumatsena said: This alliance with you was desired by me even before, but I was deprived of my kingdom, and so I held back from it.

sanskrit: abhiprāyas tv ayaṃ yo me pūrvam evābhikāṅkṣitaḥ sa nirvartatu me 'dyaiva kāṅkṣito hy asi me 'tithiḥ
english: But let that desire of mine, which was longed for even before, be fulfilled this very day; for you are a guest I have desired.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ sarvān samānīya dvijān āśramavāsinaḥ yathāvidhi samudvāhaṃ kārayām āsatur nṛpau
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, having assembled all the brahmins dwelling in the hermitage, the two kings had the marriage performed according to rite.

sanskrit: dattvā tv aśvapatiḥ kanyāṃ yathārhaṃ ca paricchadam yayau svam eva bhavanaṃ yuktaḥ paramayā mudā
english: After giving his daughter and a suitable dowry of possessions, Aśvapati returned to his own home filled with the highest joy.

sanskrit: satyavān api bhāryāṃ tāṃ labdhvā sarvaguṇānvitām mumude sā ca taṃ labdhvā bhartāraṃ manasepsitam
english: Satyavān too rejoiced upon obtaining that wife endowed with every virtue, and she rejoiced upon obtaining him as the husband she had desired in her heart.

sanskrit: gate pitari sarvāṇi saṃnyasyābharaṇāni sā jagṛhe valkalāny eva vastraṃ kāṣāyam eva ca
english: After her father departed, she put aside all her ornaments and took up only the bark garments and the ochre-colored cloth.

sanskrit: paricārair guṇaiś caiva praśrayeṇa damena ca sarvakāmakriyābhiś ca sarveṣāṃ tuṣṭim āvahat
english: By her service, her virtues, her modesty and self-restraint, and by fulfilling every desire, she won the satisfaction of all.

sanskrit: śvaśrūṃ śarīrasatkāraiḥ sarvair ācchādanādibhiḥ śvaśuraṃ devakāryaiś ca vācaḥ saṃyamanena ca
english: She pleased her mother-in-law with all the attentions to her body and with clothing and such things, and her father-in-law with the performance of divine rites and with restraint of speech.

sanskrit: tathaiva priyavādena naipuṇena śamena ca rahaś caivopacāreṇa bhartāraṃ paryatoṣayat
english: Likewise, she completely pleased her husband with pleasant speech, with skillfulness, with tranquility, and with attendance upon him in private.

sanskrit: evaṃ tatrāśrame teṣāṃ tadā nivasatāṃ satām kālas tapasyatāṃ kaś cid aticakrāma bhārata
english: Thus, O Bhārata, some time passed for those virtuous people as they dwelt in that hermitage engaged in their ascetic practices.

sanskrit: sāvitryās tu śayānāyās tiṣṭhantyāś ca divāniśam nāradena yad uktaṃ tad vākyaṃ manasi vartate
english: But for Sāvitrī, whether lying down or standing, day and night, that speech spoken by Nārada ever remained in her mind.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataḥ kāle bahutithe vyatikrānte kadā cana prāptaḥ sa kālo martavyaṃ yatra satyavatā nṛpa
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, after much time had elapsed, there arrived, O king, that moment when Satyavān was to die.

sanskrit: gaṇayantyāś ca sāvitryā divase divase gate tad vākyaṃ nāradenoktaṃ vartate hṛdi nityaśaḥ
english: And as Sāvitrī counted each passing day, that word spoken by Nārada rested perpetually in her heart.

sanskrit: caturthe 'hani martavyam iti saṃcintya bhāminī vrataṃ trirātram uddiśya divārātraṃ sthitābhavat
english: Reflecting that death was to come on the fourth day, the beautiful woman undertook a three-night vow and stood still both day and night.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā niyamaṃ duḥkhaṃ vadhvā duḥkhānvito nṛpaḥ utthāya vākyaṃ sāvitrīm abravīt parisāntvayan
english: Hearing of his daughter-in-law's painful vow, the king rose, afflicted with sorrow, and spoke words to Sāvitrī to comfort her.

sanskrit: atitīvro 'yam ārambhas tvayārabdho nṛpātmaje tisṛṇāṃ vasatīnāṃ hi sthānaṃ paramaduṣkaram
english: This undertaking you have begun is exceedingly severe, O princess; standing for three full days and nights is supremely difficult.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca na kāryas tāta saṃtāpaḥ pārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ vratam vyavasāyakṛtaṃ hīdaṃ vyavasāyaś ca kāraṇam
english: Sāvitrī said: You should not be distressed, father. I shall complete the vow; this is done by firm resolve, and resolve is the cause.

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca vrataṃ bhindhīti vaktuṃ tvāṃ nāsmi śaktaḥ kathaṃ cana pārayasveti vacanaṃ yuktam asmadvidho vadet
english: Dyumatsena said: I am in no way able to tell you to break the vow; one such as I should say only the proper word: "Complete it."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam uktvā dyumatseno virarāma mahāmanāḥ tiṣṭhantī cāpi sāvitrī kāṣṭhabhūteva lakṣyate
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, the noble-minded Dyumatsena fell silent, and Sāvitrī as she stood appeared like a wooden post.

sanskrit: śvobhūte bhartṛmaraṇe sāvitryā bharatarṣabha duḥkhānvitāyās tiṣṭhantyāś ca sā rātrir vyatyavartata
english: On the eve of her husband's death, O bull of the Bhāratas, that night passed for Sāvitrī as she stood, afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: adya tad divasaṃ ceti hutvā dīptaṃ hutāśanam yugamātrodite sūrye kṛtvā paurvāhṇikīḥ kriyāḥ
english: "Today is that day" — having offered oblations into the blazing fire, when the sun had risen a yoke's height, and having performed the morning rites,

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvān dvijān vṛddhāñ śvaśrūṃ śvaśuram eva ca abhivādyānupūrvyeṇa prāñjalir niyatā sthitā
english: she then saluted in due order all the elder twice-born, her mother-in-law, and her father-in-law, and stood with folded hands, composed.

sanskrit: avaidhavyāśiṣas te tu sāvitryarthaṃ hitāḥ śubhāḥ ūcus tapasvinaḥ sarve tapovananivāsinaḥ
english: All the ascetics dwelling in the ascetic forest then spoke auspicious blessings of non-widowhood for Sāvitrī's sake.

sanskrit: evam astv iti sāvitrī dhyānayogaparāyaṇā manasā tā giraḥ sarvāḥ pratyagṛhṇāt tapasvinām
english: "So be it" — Sāvitrī, wholly intent on meditative absorption, accepted all those words of the ascetics with her mind.

sanskrit: taṃ kālaṃ ca muhūrtaṃ ca pratīkṣantī nṛpātmajā yathoktaṃ nāradavacaś cintayantī suduḥkhitā
english: Awaiting that time and that moment, the princess thought on the words of Nārada just as he had spoken them, deeply distressed.

sanskrit: tatas tu śvaśrūśvaśurāv ūcatus tāṃ nṛpātmajām ekāntastham idaṃ vākyaṃ prītyā bharatasattama
english: Then her mother-in-law and father-in-law, O foremost of the Bhāratas, spoke these words with affection to the princess who stood apart.

sanskrit: śvaśurāv ūcatuḥ vrato yathopadiṣṭo 'yaṃ yathāvat pāritas tvayā āhārakālaḥ saṃprāptaḥ kriyatāṃ yad anantaram
english: The parents-in-law said: This vow, as it was prescribed, has been properly completed by you. The time for eating has arrived; do now what comes next.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca astaṃ gate mayāditye bhoktavyaṃ kṛtakāmayā eṣa me hṛdi saṃkalpaḥ samayaś ca kṛto mayā
english: Sāvitrī said: I shall eat after the sun has set, when my wish has been fulfilled. This is the resolve in my heart and the pledge I have made.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇāyāḥ sāvitryā bhojanaṃ prati skandhe paraśum ādāya satyavān prasthito vanam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: While Sāvitrī was thus speaking about food, Satyavān took his axe upon his shoulder and set out for the forest.

sanskrit: sāvitrī tv āha bhartāraṃ naikas tvaṃ gantum arhasi saha tvayāgamiṣyāmi na hi tvāṃ hātum utsahe
english: But Sāvitrī said to her husband: "You should not go alone. I shall go with you; I cannot bear to be separated from you."

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca vanaṃ na gatapūrvaṃ te duḥkhaḥ panthāś ca bhāmini vratopavāsakṣāmā ca kathaṃ padbhyāṃ gamiṣyasi
english: Satyavān said: You have not gone to the forest before, and the path is difficult, O beautiful one; weakened as you are by vow and fast, how will you walk on foot?

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca upavāsān na me glānir nāsti cāpi pariśramaḥ gamane ca kṛtotsāhāṃ pratiṣeddhuṃ na mārhasi
english: Sāvitrī said: I feel no fatigue from the fast, nor any weariness. I have resolved to go; you should not prevent me.

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca yadi te gamanotsāhaḥ kariṣyāmi tava priyam mama tv āmantraya gurūn na māṃ doṣaḥ spṛśed ayam
english: Satyavān said: If you are resolved on going, I shall do what pleases you; but first take leave of my elders, so that no fault may touch me.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sābhigamyābravīc chvaśrūṃ śvaśuraṃ ca mahāvratā ayaṃ gacchati me bhartā phalāhāro mahāvanam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: She who had taken the great vow approached and spoke to her mother-in-law and father-in-law: "My husband is going to the great forest for fruits."

sanskrit: iccheyam abhyanujñātum āryayā śvaśureṇa ca anena saha nirgantuṃ na hi me virahaḥ kṣamaḥ
english: "I desire to be permitted by the noble lady and by my father-in-law to go out with him; separation from him is not bearable for me."

sanskrit: gurvagnihotrārthakṛte prasthitaś ca sutas tava na nivāryo nivāryaḥ syād anyathā prasthito vanam
english: "Your son is going out for the sake of the sacred fire and the guru; he cannot be stopped. He might be stopped if he were going to the forest otherwise."

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraḥ kiṃ cid ūno na niṣkrāntāham āśramāt vanaṃ kusumitaṃ draṣṭuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: "For nearly a year I have not gone outside the hermitage; I have a great longing to see the forest in bloom."

sanskrit: dyumatsena uvāca yataḥ prabhṛti sāvitrī pitrā dattā snuṣā mama nānayābhyarthanāyuktam uktapūrvaṃ smarāmy aham
english: Dyumatsena said: Ever since Sāvitrī was given to me as a daughter-in-law by her father, I do not recall that she has ever made an improper request.

sanskrit: tad eṣā labhatāṃ kāmaṃ yathābhilaṣitaṃ vadhūḥ apramādaś ca kartavyaḥ putri satyavataḥ pathi
english: Let this daughter-in-law then obtain the wish she desires. But care must be taken, my daughter, on the path alongside Satyavān.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ubhābhyām abhyanujñātā sā jagāma yaśasvinī saha bhartrā hasantīva hṛdayena vidūyatā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Permitted by both, the illustrious Sāvitrī went forth with her husband, appearing to smile while her heart was torn with anguish.

sanskrit: sā vanāni vicitrāṇi ramaṇīyāni sarvaśaḥ mayūraravaghuṣṭāni dadarśa vipulekṣaṇā
english: The wide-eyed woman beheld the varied and delightful forests all around, resounding with the calls of peacocks.

sanskrit: nadīḥ puṇyavahāś caiva puṣpitāṃś ca nagottamān satyavān āha paśyeti sāvitrīṃ madhurākṣaram
english: The holy-flowing rivers and the blossoming trees — Satyavān kept saying to Sāvitrī in sweet words: "Look at this!"

sanskrit: nirīkṣamāṇā bhartāraṃ sarvāvastham aninditā mṛtam eva hi taṃ mene kāle munivacaḥ smaran
english: The blameless woman, watching her husband in all his moods, already regarded him as dead, recalling in that moment the sage's words.

sanskrit: anuvartatī tu bhartāraṃ jagāma mṛdugāminī dvidheva hṛdayaṃ kṛtvā taṃ ca kālam avekṣatī
english: Yet following her husband, she walked with gentle gait, as if her heart were split in two, all the while watching for that moment.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atha bhāryāsahāyaḥ sa phalāny ādāya vīryavān kaṭhinaṃ pūrayām āsa tataḥ kāṣṭhāny apāṭayat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then that valiant man, with his wife as his companion, gathered fruits and filled his basket, and afterward split firewood.

sanskrit: tasya pāṭayataḥ kāṣṭhaṃ svedo vai samajāyata vyāyāmena ca tenāsya jajñe śirasi vedanā
english: As he split the wood, sweat broke out upon him, and from the exertion he felt a pain arise in his head.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya priyāṃ bhāryām uvāca śramapīḍitaḥ vyāyāmena mamānena jātā śirasi vedanā
english: Approaching his dear wife, he said, tormented by fatigue: "From this exertion of mine a pain has arisen in my head."

sanskrit: aṅgāni caiva sāvitri hṛdayaṃ dūyatīva ca asvastham iva cātmānaṃ lakṣaye mitabhāṣiṇi
english: "And all my limbs and my heart seem to burn, O Sāvitrī, O you of measured speech; I perceive that I am unwell."

sanskrit: śūlair iva śiro viddham idaṃ saṃlakṣayāmy aham tat svaptum icche kalyāṇi na sthātuṃ śaktir asti me
english: "I perceive that my head is pierced as if by spears; I wish to sleep, O auspicious one — I have no strength to stand."

sanskrit: samāsādyātha sāvitrī bhartāram upagūhya ca utsaṅge 'sya śiraḥ kṛtvā niṣasāda mahītale
english: Then Sāvitrī approached, embraced her husband, placed his head in her lap, and sat down upon the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā nāradavaco vimṛśantī tapasvinī taṃ muhūrtaṃ kṣaṇaṃ velāṃ divasaṃ ca yuyoja ha
english: Then that ascetic woman, reflecting on Nārada's words, reckoned that moment, that instant, that hour, and that day together.

sanskrit: muhūrtād iva cāpaśyat puruṣaṃ pītavāsasam baddhamauliṃ vapuṣmantam ādityasamatejasam
english: And within a moment she saw a man clad in yellow garments, with a bound diadem, magnificent in form, with radiance equal to the sun's.

sanskrit: śyāmāvadātaṃ raktākṣaṃ pāśahastaṃ bhayāvaham sthitaṃ satyavataḥ pārśve nirīkṣantaṃ tam eva ca
english: Dark-complexioned and fair, with red eyes, a noose in his hand, inspiring dread, he stood at Satyavān's side, gazing intently at him.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya bhartur nyasya śanaiḥ śiraḥ kṛtāñjalir uvācārtā hṛdayena pravepatā
english: Seeing him, she quickly rose, gently laid her husband's head down, stood with folded hands, and spoke, distressed, her heart trembling.

sanskrit: daivataṃ tvābhijānāmi vapur etad dhy amānuṣam kāmayā brūhi me deva kas tvaṃ kiṃ ca cikīrṣasi
english: "I recognize you as a divine being, for this form is superhuman. Tell me of your own will, O god — who are you, and what do you intend to do?"

sanskrit: yama uvāca pativratāsi sāvitri tathaiva ca taponvitā atas tvām abhibhāṣāmi viddhi māṃ tvaṃ śubhe yamam
english: Yama said: "You are a devoted wife, Sāvitrī, and likewise endowed with ascetic power; therefore I address you directly. Know me, O auspicious one — I am Yama."

sanskrit: ayaṃ te satyavān bhartā kṣīṇāyuḥ pārthivātmajaḥ neṣyāmy enam ahaṃ baddhvā viddhy etan me cikīrṣitam
english: "This Satyavān, your husband, the son of a king, has exhausted his lifespan; I shall bind him and lead him away — know this to be my intention."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ity uktvā pitṛrājas tāṃ bhagavān svaṃ cikīrṣitam yathāvat sarvam ākhyātuṃ tatpriyārthaṃ pracakrame
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, the blessed lord of the fathers began to explain fully his entire intention for her sake, wishing to please her.

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi dharmasaṃyukto rūpavān guṇasāgaraḥ nārho matpuruṣair netum ato 'smi svayam āgataḥ
english: "For this man is endowed with righteousness, handsome, an ocean of virtues; he is not fit to be led away by my messengers — therefore I have come myself."

sanskrit: tataḥ satyavataḥ kāyāt pāśabaddhaṃ vaśaṃ gatam aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ niścakarṣa yamo balāt
english: Then Yama forcibly drew from the body of Satyavān the thumb-sized person bound with a noose, come under his sway.

sanskrit: tataḥ samuddhṛtaprāṇaṃ gataśvāsaṃ hataprabham nirviceṣṭaṃ śarīraṃ tad babhūvāpriyadarśanam
english: Then that body, its life-breath extracted, its breath gone, its lustre lost, motionless — became a pitiable sight to behold.
